short_title: IFMS-OCC Interface ICD (IF and Modem System)
organisation: MakaluMedia Internet & Engineering Services GmbH, Darmstadt (for ESA/ESOC)

summary:
The interface control document for the file-based data interface of the **IFMS** (Intermediate Frequency and Modem System), the ranging, Doppler and receiver equipment in ESA's ESTRACK ground stations. The interface serves data clients such as [NCTRS](../scos2000/nctrs-nis.md) and, for historical reasons, is called the IFMS-to-OCC (Operations Control Centre) interface. It carries radiometric and station measurement data, not TM/TC frames.

The IFMS acts as a read-only FTP server over TCP/IP. The document lists the supported FTP commands and profile (stream mode, file structure, ASCII and image types only). Clients get catalogue access through directory listings, off-line access by retrieval, and 'pseudo-on-line' access through small data-sets that cover short measurement durations. Data-sets sit under `<data_set_root>/station/spacecraft/`, and their file names encode station, spacecraft, year, day of year, data-set kind, DAP (data acquisition process) type, DAP start time and a sequence number. DAP types are D1/D2 (Doppler), G1/G2 (AGC), ME (meteo), RG (ranging) and OL (open loop). Gzip copies and '.raw' uncorrected ranging files are also covered.

Section 6 defines the content of each data-set. The header holds station, spacecraft, time tags, requestor (DCP or STC), why the file was opened, sample period, carrier and tone indicators and a dump of the active configuration table. The measurement records are: Doppler (NCO count, unwrapped phase and the derived one-way delta delay, with the full algorithm for coherent and non-coherent transponders), AGC (carrier level, polarisation, channel powers, lock status), meteo (humidity, pressure, temperature), ranging (delay, code number, ambiguity flag, DSP status) and binary open-loop records (a 44-byte header with magic number 0xA3C725B6 and 136 six-byte blocks of packed I/Q samples). Section 7 covers the Support-Log files and section 8 the user access rules. The annexes give the BNF syntax and example files. The copy comes from the Mars Express radio science archive.

key_points.text: Change history highlights: Open-Loop data-sets added in 10.2.0 (2004-03-29), a 'freqplan' configuration table added to the header in 10.3.0, IP/X.25 mentions removed and new AGC measurements added in 10.5.0, 'gmdemod' header parameters added in 10.6.0.
The ICD describes the interface between the IFMS and data clients such as NCTRS; for historical reasons it is known as the IFMS-to-OCC (Operations Control Centre) interface.

The interface is entirely standard FTP over TCP/IP with read-only files; the IFMS FTP server supports USER, PASS, QUIT, PORT, MODE (S only), TYPE (A and I only), STRU (F only), CWD, PWD, LIST and RETR.

Pseudo-on-line delivery uses small data files of short measurement duration, set by configuration parameters (D1MaxDs, D2MaxDs, G1MaxDs, G2MaxDs, MeMaxDs, RgMaxDs); technically it is identical to off-line access.

File names such as PER1_CLU3_2002_108_OP_RG_145513_0001 encode station ID, spacecraft ID, year, day of year, data-set kind, DAP type (D1, D2, G1, G2, ME, OL, RG), DAP start time hhmmss and a 4-digit sequence ID; nominal length 31 characters.

Maximum DAP duration is 20 hours (72000 s); uncorrected ranging data are kept as '.raw' files in a 'raw/' subdirectory, and in this issue the IFMS software does not yet correct ranging data, so only raw files exist.
Field types are B (Boolean), F (Float), I (Integer), S (String) and T (Time, 'YYYYMMDD.hhmmss.mmm'), with units in < > and accuracy in [ ].

The data-set header includes requestor_id (DCP or STC), why_opened (DAP_Started, Conf_Change, Max_Size_Reached, Tone_Lost), sample_period, carrier and tone indicators, epd_source, rg_data_corrected and the active configuration (modulator, freqplan, tracking, rcdemod, scdemod, gmdemod).

Doppler records hold sample number and time, a 17.5 MHz NCO interval count, unwrapped carrier phase (turns), a spurious-carrier flag and the one-way delta delay; the ICD gives the delta-delay derivation for coherent and non-coherent transponders.
Ranging records hold the round-trip delay modulo the code ambiguity, the current code number (1 to 24), ambiguity-resolution and spurious flags, estimated Doppler (KD-1) and DSP status values.

Open-loop records come from the GDSP 17.5 Msps complex baseband stream; each record has a 44-byte big-endian header (magic 0xA3C725B6) and 136 blocks of 6 bytes holding 12, 6, 3 or 1 samples for 1, 2, 4 or 12-bit quantisation; a new data-set opens every minute.
Six Support-Log files (D1, D2, G1, G2, ME, RG) in ~ifmsdset/support_logs/ log data-set open, close and delete events; they are intended only as a backup monitoring mechanism.
External FTP users can never create, modify or delete files; data-set deletion is controlled only through the DCP and STC interfaces.

notes: The file comes from the Mars Express radio-science (MRS) dataset in ESA's Planetary Science Archive (IFMS_OCCFTP.PDF), but the document is generic ESTRACK IFMS documentation, not specific to Mars Express. Section 8.1 prints a default FTP account name and password; they are deliberately not reproduced here. The change history entries for 10.3.0 refer to '[SUM]' and '[ADD]', and §5.2 to '[IFMS_SUM]', while the reference list names '[IFMS-SUM]'. Table 2 is numbered twice (Doppler and AGC). The worked file-name example says the DAP started on 1999-04-18 at 14:55:13, but the file name shows 2002 and 145513. The extraction reports 28 PDF pages (registry: 27); the last is empty. STC and DCP are not expanded in this document.
